title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-profit-target-weekly-channel PR #222 review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's fresh full review of PR #222 (backend-profit-target-weekly-channel), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: This one PR's stale-daily-channel-copy bug has now recurred across 5 separate locations over 2 review rounds (frontend/src/utils/profitTargetHelpText.ts, both features/{stocks,portfolio}/components/metricHelpContent.ts, backend/app/api/schemas.py's ProfitTargetOut.source, and docs/architecture/API.md's profit_target paragraph) -- each fix pass caught the previously-named locations but missed at least one more. Worth a lightweight, cheap guard against a 6th recurrence: e.g. a small unit/doc test (or a simple grep-based check run in CI/static-verify) asserting that every place describing suggest_profit_target's channel source uses 'weekly'/'weeks' wording and never 'today'/'daily'/'100 days' -- so this specific bug class is caught by tooling next time a related change touches this metric, rather than depending on a human/reviewer re-grepping the whole repo by hand each time.

A 6th instance of this bug class was found and fixed during the final (accepted) review round: frontend/src/features/methodology/data/methodologyContent.ts's profit-target entry summary. Note that methodologyContent.test.ts (unlike profitTargetHelpText.test.ts and both metricHelpContent.test.ts files) only asserts structural invariants (non-empty fields, unique ids) and has no content-specific regression test guarding this string against reverting to 'daily'/'today's' wording -- worth folding into the same guard as the item above, or adding a dedicated assertion, rather than relying solely on manual review to keep it correct going forward.

docs/ideas.md's 'Surface suggested stop-loss/profit-target more prominently for open positions' idea entry -- specifically its 'Correction from reading ch. 39 "Triple Screen Trading System" directly (p. 161...)' bullet -- still states in the present tense that 'suggest_profit_target's channel/support-resistance target ... [is] computed entirely off daily data', which is now stale: the channel candidate moved to weekly as of this PR. Non-blocking (docs/ideas.md is an explicit scratch pad per its own header, not one of CLAUDE.md's designated source-of-truth docs, and this task's own decisions record treats analogous historical text -- docs/tasks/done/backend-profit-target.json -- as an intentionally-preserved record rather than a living doc), but worth a follow-up pass to either update the bullet to reflect the fix or note it's now resolved, so a future reader of docs/ideas.md isn't misled about current behavior.

decisions.decision: Built the checklist item 1 guard as a new stdlib-only script, `scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py` (mirroring `scripts/validate_tasks.py`'s own zero-setup convention, with its own `scripts/tests/test_check_profit_target_wording.py` unit-test file, 17 tests), and wired it into the `static-verify` skill as a new step 5 -- rather than a one-off manual grep, a bespoke pytest-only test living in `backend/tests/` (which wouldn't cover frontend/docs prose), or a brand-new dedicated skill. Chose `static-verify` specifically because both `pr-reviewer` and `task-qa-reviewer` already run it unconditionally on every task, giving this guard real teeth against a 7th recurrence without requiring anyone to remember a separate command -- this repo has no CI config at all (no `.github/workflows`), so 'run in CI/static-verify' (the checklist item's own suggested phrasing) resolves to static-verify as the closest real equivalent. The script does two things: (1) a repo-wide negative grep for the exact recurring wording ('today's Autoenvelope', 'that day's Autoenvelope', '~100 days of history') across backend/frontend/docs, catching a literal regression anywhere including a brand-new file; (2) a positive per-file check against a curated list of the 8 locations this bug class has actually touched (the 6 it already hit, plus profit_target.py and the source-of-truth schemas.py field), requiring each to still say 'weekly'/'week' wherever it describes the channel/Autoenvelope candidate -- catching a future paraphrase that dodges the literal banned wording. Two of those 8 files (`features/portfolio/components/metricHelpContent.ts`, `methodologyContent.ts`) needed an explicit anchor (start/end regex scoping to just the relevant object/entry) rather than a plain whole-file windowed check, since both files also correctly describe a completely different, still-DAILY metric (trade grading's entry-day channel) close enough by that an unscoped context window produced false positives against that unrelated, correct prose -- verified this both by running the script against the real repo (caught the false positives, then confirmed clean after scoping) and via a dedicated regression test (`test_anchor_scoping_ignores_unrelated_daily_metric_elsewhere_in_file`). `docs/tasks/` (both active and `done/`) and `docs/ideas.md` are hard-excluded from the guard entirely -- both legitimately quote the banned wording verbatim as historical/scratch-pad record (this task's own checklist text, and `docs/tasks/done/backend-profit-target-weekly-channel.json`'s `decisions`/`review` fields, contain the literal banned phrases describing the bug itself) rather than describing current behavior, consistent with the parent task's own established precedent for treating task-board JSON as an immutable record, not living documentation. Test files (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`) are also excluded from the negative check, since 4 of them (the 3 pre-existing ones plus this task's new methodologyContent.test.ts assertion) intentionally reference the banned wording as a regex literal inside a negative assertion -- that's the guard already working at the unit-test level, not a regression to flag.
decisions.rationale: Rejected a single project-wide regex without any file-scoping/curated-list distinction (i.e. just grep the whole repo for 'daily' near 'channel'/'Autoenvelope' near 'profit target') -- tried this first and it produced immediate false positives against schemas.py's/API.md's/profit_target.py's own CORRECT current wording, which explicitly and correctly contrasts the weekly profit-target channel against the daily `channel_upper`/`channel_lower` indicator in the same sentence (e.g. 'a different channel than the daily one AnalysisResponse.indicators.channel_upper/channel_lower expose') -- a naive 'daily near channel' ban would have permanently blocked ever writing that necessary disambiguating sentence again. Rejected excluding `docs/ideas.md` from the guard AND leaving its stale text alone (i.e. treating checklist items 1 and 3 as fully independent) -- since ideas.md's own explicit 'not a source-of-truth doc' status is exactly why it's guard-exempt, not a reason to skip fixing it manually; did both (guard-exempt AND manually fixed, per item 3). Considered writing this as a Vitest-side check instead (frontend already runs a test suite on every relevant file) -- rejected since half the known locations (profit_target.py, schemas.py, docs/Analyse.md, docs/architecture/API.md) aren't scannable from a Vitest process without an awkward cross-language dependency; a standalone Python script scanning by file extension needs no such boundary and matches `validate_tasks.py`'s own precedent for a cross-cutting repo check living outside either app's own test runner.

comments.summary: Non-blocking: check_banned_patterns() scans per physical line, so it misses a banned phrase split across lines by Python implicit string concatenation -- a style already used elsewhere in backend/app/api/schemas.py's own IndicatorsOut field descriptions. Verified directly this defeats the negative check for a synthetic wrapped example. However, verified the per-file positive check (check_known_files_mention_weekly, character-window-based, not per-line) independently still catches a reversion in any of the 8 known files regardless of line-wrapping -- confirmed by reverting schemas.py's actual `source` field to the old stale wording, wrapped, and observing the negative check miss it while the positive check still flagged it. Only a live gap for a hypothetical brand-new file outside the known list. Tracked on the followups-of-followups task.

Non-blocking: _WEEKLY_RE = re.compile(r'\bweek(ly)?\b') doesn't match the plural 'weeks' alone (verified: _WEEKLY_RE.search('100 weeks') is None). Currently harmless since every real occurrence in the repo pairs 'weeks' with 'weekly' nearby, but could false-positive-flag a future, fully-correct edit that only says 'weeks'. Only causes false positives (annoying, self-revealing), never a false negative on the actual bug this guard exists to catch. Tracked on the followups-of-followups task.

Non-blocking: _iter_scanned_files() walks the entire repo tree via rglob('*') before filtering excluded directory names, rather than pruning node_modules/.venv/.git during traversal -- wasteful and will get slower as those grow, given this now runs on every static-verify invocation (every PR review, every task QA pass). Tracked on the followups-of-followups task.

Non-blocking: _PROFIT_TARGET_CONTEXT_RE's `profit[\s_]target` alternative doesn't match the hyphenated 'profit-target' text of methodologyContent.ts's own start_anchor. Verified the anchor text alone doesn't match; the check currently passes only because the same entry's `name` field independently contains 'Profit Target' (a genuine structural field, not throwaway prose, so lower practical fragility than it first appears, but still an unnecessary gap). Tracked on the followups-of-followups task.

Non-blocking: _extract_region() silently falls back to scanning to end-of-file when end_anchor fails to match, with no violation/warning emitted -- asymmetric with the explicit violation raised when start_anchor fails to match. A future structural change that breaks an end anchor (e.g. profitTargetHelp becoming the last export) would silently balloon the scanned region into unrelated trailing content with no signal to update the guard. Tracked on the followups-of-followups task.

Non-blocking: scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py has one ruff finding (SIM103, a trivial if/return simplification) that its sibling scripts/validate_tasks.py -- which it explicitly mirrors -- doesn't have. Neither script is part of the enforced backend ruff gate, so non-blocking, but worth tidying for consistency. Tracked on the followups-of-followups task.

review.notes:
Full review of PR #223 (backend-profit-target-weekly-channel-followups). Verified the guard script's actual claims rather than trusting the task-worker's report:

(1) Empirically confirmed all 6 real PR #222 regressions would have been caught: reconstructed each pre-fix historical file content directly from git history (b493a7a for schemas.py, c502aaa~1 for the three frontend copy locations, cfaface~1 for API.md and methodologyContent.ts) and ran check_banned_patterns() against the real historical text for each -- every one of the 6 produced a banned-pattern violation (verified with the actual regexes, not just by reading the test suite).

(2) Empirically confirmed the anchor scoping on features/portfolio/components/metricHelpContent.ts and methodologyContent.ts both (a) produces zero false positives against their real current content (ran check_known_files_mention_weekly() against the real repo -- clean), and (b) is load-bearing, not decorative: removed the anchors and re-ran against the same real files -- both then produced exactly the false positive the anchor exists to prevent (metricHelpContent.ts's tradeGradeHelp ~100-bar warm-up text; methodologyContent.ts's trade-grading entry summary), confirming the anchors are doing real, necessary work, not just adding complexity for no benefit. Also confirmed schemas.py and profit_target.py (both unanchored, whole-file-scanned) don't need anchoring themselves: per-occurrence instrumentation showed their own nearby daily-channel mentions (channel_upper/channel_lower field docs, trade-grading TradeOut fields) correctly never pair with profit-target context within the 700-char window, so they're safe without one.

(3) Confirmed docs/tasks/ (including docs/tasks/done/) and docs/ideas.md exclusions are scoped by exact Path equality/parents check, not string-prefix matching, so no accidental over-exclusion of a similarly-named path; confirmed docs/Analyse.md and docs/architecture/API.md (the two source-of-truth docs that DO need checking) are not excluded and are actively scanned.

(4) Confirmed static-verify wiring: the new step 5 is unconditional (not gated behind any 'if area is X' branch) in .claude/skills/static-verify/SKILL.md, correctly renumbered (old steps 5/6 -> 6/7), and the 'four commands' -> 'five commands' note was updated to match -- both pr-reviewer and task-qa-reviewer load this skill on every task, so this guard genuinely runs going forward without anyone needing to remember a separate command.

Ran the full project checks: backend pytest --cov, 1102 passed, 99.95% coverage (gate 90%, no regression). Frontend vitest --coverage, 708 passed across 71 files (2 more than PR #222's 706, from the new methodologyContent.test.ts cases), 99.72%/99.19%/99.72%/99.78% stmt/branch/fn/line (no regression). Backend ruff+mypy clean (backend/app/ scope, unaffected by this PR anyway). Frontend eslint+tsc -b --noEmit clean. The new profit-target guard script itself: clean against the real repo (218 files + 8 known locations, zero violations). scripts/validate_tasks.py: board validates cleanly (245 task files after filing the followups-of-followups task below, no violations) including this task's own new git/decisions/checklist updates and the review/state/path updates made by this review.

No API/schema change in this PR -- OpenAPI snapshot check not applicable. No new frontend production component (only a test file, frontend/src/features/methodology/data/methodologyContent.test.ts) -- placement-decision check (7a) not applicable. This PR is not UI-facing: touches only a new repo-root script + its stdlib unittest suite, the static-verify skill doc, a docs/ideas.md wording fix, and task-board JSON -- no application code (backend or frontend production source) changed at all. Skipping the browser walkthrough (step 9) and the persisted e2e suite (step 9a) explicitly for this reason rather than silently omitting them. area is backend/signals (inherited from the parent task) but no signal/confidence/risk code is touched by this diff, so verify-elder-signal's methodology-conformance check has no surface to apply to here; docs/Analyse.md itself is unchanged and was already independently reviewed in PR #222's cycle. Not loading architecture-review either: the one new script mirrors scripts/validate_tasks.py's own established convention (stdlib-only, repo-root, not part of the enforced ruff/mypy gate) rather than introducing a new module/dependency/layer.

Code-review skill (medium effort, run as a background subagent) returned 4 findings; independently re-verified all 4 by direct construction/execution rather than taking them at face value, and additionally verified (by reverting schemas.py's real `source` field to the old stale wording in a wrapped/multi-line style and re-running both checks) that the per-file positive check still catches what the repo-wide negative check's line-based scanning misses -- meaning none of the 4 findings, nor the 2 I found independently (asymmetric end-anchor fallback; one ruff SIM103 nit), actually let a real regression in any of the 8 known locations through undetected. All 6 are genuine, verified robustness gaps in a brand-new internal tooling script, but none reach the 'correctness bug that defeats this PR's actual purpose' bar -- filed as followups rather than blocking.

Task-board cross-check: all three checklist items correctly marked done and match the actual delivered work; the single decisions entry substantively documents what was built, why static-verify was chosen as the wiring point, why the two anchors were needed, and three explicitly-rejected alternatives with rationale -- no checklist item phrased as 'decide X' lacks a decision. No open questions. git.pr_number/pr_url correctly recorded. index.json state mirror is correct (testing).

Verdict: accepted. Filed docs/tasks/backend-profit-target-weekly-channel-followups-followups.json for the 6 non-blocking findings above (checked index.json first -- no existing follow-up-of-followup task for this id).

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-verified pr-reviewer's accept. Re-ran full suites myself: backend pytest --cov 1102 passed / 99.95% coverage, frontend vitest --coverage 708 passed across 71 files / 99.72-99.78% stmt-branch-fn-line, scripts/tests/test_check_profit_target_wording.py 17/17, ruff+mypy+eslint+tsc all clean, scripts/validate_tasks.py clean -- all match the review's reported numbers exactly. Reconstructed 6/6 (not just 2) of the original PR #222 pre-fix regressions from git history (b493a7a for schemas.py, c502aaa~1 for the three frontend copy locations, cfaface~1 for API.md and methodologyContent.ts) and ran check_banned_patterns() against each -- every one genuinely flags a violation. Confirmed the anchor-scoping on the two nearby-daily-content files (portfolio metricHelpContent.ts, methodologyContent.ts) is clean against real content and, by removing the anchors and re-running, confirmed it's load-bearing (produces exactly the false positive against the unrelated trade-grading daily text the anchor exists to prevent). Confirmed static-verify/SKILL.md step 5 genuinely invokes `python3 scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py` unconditionally, correctly renumbered, with the four->five commands note updated to match -- not just a prose mention. Skimmed the full diff (SKILL.md, docs/ideas.md, methodologyContent.test.ts, the new script + its test suite, task-board JSON) and found nothing pr-reviewer underweighted; the followups-of-followups task's 6 items are all genuine and already correctly filed as non-blocking. Accept holds.
